note: Informational record of the bug CATEGORIES the hidden oracle (oracle_test.ts, written transiently by grader.py) checks for. The builder writes distributeCatchUpFlush() from scratch -- nothing is literally injected into its code. 'Seeded' here means 'plausible implementation mistakes a cheap builder model might make against this exact spec', which is what the oracle is designed to catch independent of whatever the spec-writer's own acceptance tests happened to cover.

bugs.description: day1Date computed as missDate + 0 days (i.e. missDate itself) instead of +1, shifting all three dates one day early.

Date math done via missDate.getTime() + N * 86400000 instead of calendar-day arithmetic -- breaks across a DST transition (not exercised by the oracle, which uses UTC dates deliberately to make this specific bug class moot in THIS task) but more importantly often silently breaks month/year rollover handling if implemented via raw millisecond math on a local-time Date without normalizing to UTC first.

Splits ayahIds into three contiguous thirds (first third -> day1, etc.) instead of round-robin on index % 3 -- satisfies the 'even distribution' property but violates the exact assignment the spec requires, and differs observably from round-robin for any input where order matters to the caller.
Uses (i % 3) but assigns 0->day3, 1->day1, 2->day2 (or some other rotation) instead of 0->day1, 1->day2, 2->day3.
An off-by-one in a loop bound drops the last ayah, or an incorrect push/concat duplicates one ayah into two days.
Implementation sorts or splices the input ayahIds array in place instead of leaving it untouched (a correctness smell even when output happens to be right).
